extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors submitting manuscripts to HarperCollins (traditional publishing hopefuls)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for preparing and submitting a manuscript or proposal to HarperCollins, covering manuscript formatting, query letter content, submission mechanics, follow-up timing, and revision after rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you send your manuscript, familiarize yourself with HarperCollins' submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instructions will help you understand what the editors are looking for and how to present your work professionally. Check imprint-specific pages so you know particular preferences or required materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard font
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a standard font like Times New Roman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a conventional, readable font demonstrates professionalism and makes the manuscript easy for editors to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-space the text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-spacing improves readability for editors and reviewers and is a common submission expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your document has numbered pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page numbers help editors reference sections and prevent confusion if pages are separated or reordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a complete manuscript for fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: HarperCollins typically requires full manuscripts for fiction submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send partial or sample chapters unless a specific imprint explicitly requests them; a complete manuscript shows readiness for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a detailed proposal for non-fiction when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-fiction works, a detailed proposal may suffice, but check the specific requirements for your genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-fiction imprints often want a proposal (outline, sample chapters, marketing hook) instead of a full manuscript — confirm imprint expectations before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a concise, compelling query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: The query letter should include a brief synopsis of your book, your credentials as an author, and why your book is a good fit for HarperCollins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it concise and engaging; focus on the unique elements of your story or subject matter and highlight any relevant experience or accolades that add credibility. The goal is to capture the editor's attention quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight unique elements and author credentials in the query
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the unique elements of your story or subject matter and highlight any relevant experience or accolades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the query to demonstrate why your book stands out and why you are qualified to write it; avoid long digressions or irrelevant personal history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the correct submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: HarperCollins accepts submissions both via email and through their online portal, depending on the imprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure you double-check which method is preferred for your specific genre or imprint before sending your materials to avoid mis-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and label files correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting electronically, ensure that all files are correctly formatted and labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper file naming and format (e.g., .doc/.docx or as requested) prevents technical issues and makes it easy for editors to locate and open your materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a cover letter as instructed
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter in the body of the email or as an attachment, based on the guidelines provided by HarperCollins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the imprint's instruction about where to place the cover letter. Failure to follow these instructions can delay review or cause your submission to be overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be patient; follow up after an appropriate interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait at least three months before following up on your submission status unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't received a response within the suggested timeframe, a polite follow-up email is acceptable. Include your original query details to help the editor locate your submission quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle rejection constructively and revise
rubrics_metrics.description: If HarperCollins declines your manuscript, take the opportunity to revise and improve it based on any feedback they provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider seeking feedback from writing groups or professional editors to gain additional perspectives. Persistence and dedication are crucial; use rejection as a chance to strengthen your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate professionalism and attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Present your submission professionally to demonstrate attention to detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to formatting, submission instructions, clear labeling, and concise communication signals that you are a serious, professional author and improves the chance your work will be considered.
